reason: Conversation 1 correctly identified the door interlock/latch path as the leading suspect from the opener, gave the sensible first steps (clean latch hooks, check door closes squarely), asked a genuinely discriminating question (do fan/light/turntable stop too), stayed honest that an engineer must confirm which part is at fault, and gave proportionate safety guidance with no casing removal. Conversation 2 wasted the first turn on irrelevant checks (power level, mode, whether the cook had started), then pushed an unsupported 'overheat cut-out' theory that the customer had to correct, and ignored the clear door-switch evidence by refusing to update its diagnosis in the final turn. Both kept safety boundaries, but Conversation 2 misdiagnosed and offered no useful front-of-unit checks when asked.
